summary.text: A 59-year-old man with nitrate-responsive angina was referred to the emergency room. About 7 years earlier he had undergone coronary angiography for chest pain without a provocation test and with no significant coronary artery disease, and his angina remained uncontrolled despite several antianginal and other medications. Vital signs, examination and cardiac enzymes showed no abnormal findings.

MDCTA without nitrate during ongoing chest pain on the first hospital day showed diffuse luminal narrowing in the LAD, mid-RCA and LCX, and echocardiography showed slightly decreased LV GLS with a normal ejection fraction. CAG with ergonovine provocation induced diffuse spasm with more than 90% narrowing, which resolved after intracoronary nitroglycerine, and vasospastic angina was diagnosed.

LV GLS improved from -14.8% to -19.6% after nitroglycerine injection. The patient was discharged with additional isosorbide mononitrate and amlodipine, and there were no further recurrences of angina.

summary.text: A 70-year-old male with hypertension and angina visited the cardiology outpatient department with severe chest pain associated with alcohol consumption and frequent worsening pain despite high-dose diltiazem and isosorbide mononitrate. CAG several years earlier without provocation test had shown no significant coronary atherosclerotic disease. He was hospitalized after stopping his medical treatments for 5 days; admission ECG showed sinus rhythm and incomplete right bundle branch block, and serial troponin levels were negative.

On the day after admission MDCTA without nitrate showed multifocal luminal narrowing without definite plaque in the LAD, RCA, LCX and diagonal and obtuse marginal arteries, and echocardiography showed significantly decreased LV GLS with a 62% ejection fraction. CAG with ergonovine provocation induced total occlusion of the proximal RCA after the first 10 µg dose; nitroglycerin was unresponsive with chest pain and sinus bradycardia below 40 b.p.m.

Three additional intracoronary nitroglycerine injections restored sinus rhythm and resolved symptoms, and the final CAG showed complete recovery of coronary flow. LV GLS improved from -14.8% to -20.1% after nitrate administration. S-amlodipine 2.5 mg daily replaced diltiazem, alcohol abstinence was recommended, and he had no recurrence of chest pain with controlled blood pressure.

article_limitations: Two case reports (Case 1 and Case 2 headings in the source); Discussion statements are copied to both patients only where the sentence explicitly covers "both" or "neither of the two patients".

Table 1 labels its data "at admission", while the case text places the baseline echocardiography the day after admission and the Discussion says MDCTA and baseline echocardiography were performed on the same day; no single time is assigned to the baseline GLS.

Follow-up echocardiography is described after intracoronary nitroglycerine (Case 1 text), after nitrate administration (Case 2 text and Table 1) and after intravenous infusion of nitrate within 24 h of CAG (Discussion); the nitrate route is not assigned.
Table 1 units are kept as printed (for example troponin I in ng/L with values below 1 and NT-proBNP in pg/mL); nothing is converted and no flag is assigned from the printed normal intervals.
Case 1 initial ECG states T wave flattening or inversion; neither is asserted (review_only).
The supplementary video (sup1) is a PMC-hosted MP4 reviewed by sampled frames in the supplement manifest; audio and continuous motion were not reviewed and no clinical facts are taken from it.

The source lists one further unassigned inline image (ytaf401il1.jpg); the raw XML places it as an inline graphic in the Lead author biography section, and the parent viewed it (MD5 matched the PMC manifest): a non-clinical author portrait, not patient content. It is not a figure, not attributed to either case and not described further.
Figure pixels are inspected in visual.json; images carry printed segment strain values and burned-in identifiers in some panels (flagged in the privacy sidecar, never copied).
